tagline: The white city at the meeting of two rivers — a fortress-fortress skyline, floating nightclub barges, and the Balkans' biggest grill tables.
overview: Belgrade means 'white city' — named for the walls of Kalemegdan Fortress rising above the confluence of the Sava and Danube. The fortress park remains the city's living room, its ramparts busy with sunset-watchers.

The city's energy is famous across the Balkans: Skadarlija's cobbled bohemian quarter sings until late over grilled ćevapi and rakija, the Savamala warehouse district turned into art spaces, and hundreds of splavovi — floating raft clubs — line the rivers for summer nightlife.
Speed's 2024 tour streamed from Belgrade. History runs deep here: the city has been destroyed and rebuilt over 40 times across 7,000 years of settlement.
